audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts are shifted one stage out of step with their own why-text. Content win[0] said Skill while whys[0] says Kennen pokes you for free; win[1] and win[2] said Kennen while both whys say 'even' and 'a wash'; win[4] and win[5] said Skill/Kennen while the whys describe a true all-in and a Riftmaker burst that kills him.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Kennen/Skill/Skill/Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Kennen, which is what the prose already argues: he owns level 1, the lane levels out once Drunken Rage and Body Slam exist, Gragas owns 6 through first item, Kennen takes it back late.
audit.corrected: Content chart flipped as one group to Kennen, Skill, Skill, Skill, Gragas, Gragas, Kennen; full-layer phases matched to it with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lightning Rush is called 'a long cooldown' in three places. It is 10/9/8/7/6 — ten seconds at rank 1 and six at rank 5.
audit.why: Advice built on him being unable to escape for a long time is wrong, and a player who commits E on that belief dies. The real window is narrow: burst him inside those ten seconds, not at leisure.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in: Lightning Rush 10s at rank 1 down to 6s, Thundering Shuriken 7s at rank 1 down to 4s, Slicing Maelstrom a flat 120s, Body Slam 14s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's interaction text is generic boilerplate — 'his key tool is down', 'E-Q burst him' — and never states the two interactions that decide the fight: Mark of the Storm needing three stacks to stun, and Explosive Cask knocking Kennen out of his own ultimate.
audit.why: Riot's text: Kennen stuns after three marks, and Q, W and E each apply one. So the stun is countable — you can see it coming two marks out, and W's active only marks a target that is ALREADY marked. Slicing Maelstrom strikes enemies within 550 of Kennen, so Cask's knockback removes you from it or removes him from your team; it is the single highest-value use of a 100s ultimate in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Mark counting and the Cask-vs-Maelstrom displacement written into the interactions block and the don'ts.

audit.why: The packet flagged 'Drunken Rage's' in early as a probable wrong name. It is not — Drunken Rage is Gragas's real W. False positive, left alone.

edits.before: Kennen owns the first two levels — his Q shuriken and energized W autos poke you down before Happy Hour even exists, and with only Barrel Roll learned you have no sustain trigger to answer it. Do not walk up to throw a Q he just sidesteps with move speed; last-hit with the edge of the cask and accept some chip. The whole lane is built around catching him with E once his escape is down — drink W first so you tank the energized autos on the way in.

notes: 'Long cooldown' on Lightning Rush was wrong in three places — it is 10s at rank 1 and 6s at rank 5; corrected everywhere it drove advice. Mark of the Storm's three-stack stun and the Cask-knocks-him-out-of-Maelstrom interaction were both absent from the page and are the two facts that most change how this lane is played; added. Charts on both layers were one stage out of step with their own why-text and are flipped as an atomic group to the packet. Packet flagged 'Drunken Rage's' as a suspect name — false positive, that is Gragas's real W.
